title: Umbra Data Labs - self-serve velocity and credit pathfinding
summary: Initial PLG/self-serve discovery focused on how fast Umbra can get to first token using Redwood's hosted API, questions about free credits, and early security constraints for a potential pilot. SE provided rough latency/cost tradeoffs and recommended a two-week credit-backed spike on hosted with a follow-up technical deep dive for dedicated/private options if SLA or compliance needs arise.
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-08 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Kim (Redwood AE), Samira Ortiz (Redwood SE), Tomas Becker (Redwood CSM), Ethan Ward (Umbra CTO), Priya Malhotra (Umbra Head of ML), Liam O'Connor (Umbra Eng Mgr), Nadia (PM)

00:00 Jordan: Ok, thanks everyone for carving time. quick intro — I'm Jordan, AE on the Redwood platform. We'll run through the self-serve path, credits, and what it looks like to go from zero to first token. Samira is our SE, she'll jump into latency/cost numbers and an example integration.
00:12 Ethan: Hey thanks, appreciate it. High level we want to prototype an assistant that helps analysts query internal docs. Key constraints: PII redaction is a must, and we need to understand time to first token — how quickly can our engineers unblock?
00:25 Samira: Great. So with the hosted API our typical TTFT, time-to-first-token, for a standard web dev is mostly on the order of hours to get a working call, a day to wire up auth and a more production-like pipeline. For PLG teams we often see first call in under 30 minutes using the SDK and our quickstart. But that assumes no corporate SSO gating the sign-up.
00:41 Priya: When you say under 30 minutes, are you including data ingestion for docs? Our use case will need embeddings + search within the first sprint.
00:49 Samira: Good call. The 30-minute number is strictly for a basic generation request to the hosted endpoint using sample prompts. For embeddings + vector store hookup expect a couple hours if you already have an ingestion pipeline. We can provide a sample notebook and pre-built ingestion scripts.
01:05 Liam: And the credits piece — what does the free trial look like for a team of four? Enough to run iterative tests?
01:12 Jordan: We issue trial credits tied to the account — usually 5,000 to 50,000 tokens worth depending on partner/intent. For a focused two-week spike we can grant N credits (Jordan paraphrases an amount) — for this call let's say 50k tokens and a separate eval quota for embeddings. We can also provision a sandbox environment with higher throttles for short windows.
01:30 Ethan: Is that something we can self-serve from signup or do we need sales to enable?
01:34 Jordan: You can self-serve up to a baseline amount, but for larger trial grants we typically do a quick handoff. I'll put an enablement request on the account and Tomas will follow up to make sure the credits are provisioned.
01:46 Tomas: I'll create the ticket after this call and send the instructions for the quickstart repo.
01:52 Speaker 1: (mumbles)
02:00 Samira: On hosted vs dedicated vs private — primary tradeoffs: hosted is the fastest to get started (PLG), lowest friction, we manage key infra and updates. Dedicated gives you fixed capacity and lower tail-latency under sustained throughput; private (VPC/on-prem) is for strict compliance requirements and data residency. For your PII concerns, hosted can be configured with customer-managed KMS and retention policies, but if policy requires full network isolation that's where private comes in.
02:30 Priya: Do you have SOC2/ISO attestation and audit logs we can show security?
02:36 Jordan: Yes, SOC 2 Type II is available. We also expose audit logs per account and provide SSO/SAML and granular RBAC for console and API keys. I'll share the security package after the call.
02:48 Priya: Also curious about KV cache and context windows — our documents can be long, how do you handle long contexts?
02:55 Samira: We handle long contexts with automatic windowing and prefix caching; if you need chunking for retrieval augmented generation, our recommendations are in the quickstart. For very long single-document contexts we recommend embeddings + retrieval or a specialized model variant with longer context.
03:13 Ethan: Another practical question — if we prototype on hosted and then need to move to dedicated, how painful is the migration?
03:20 Samira: Migration is designed to be painless from an API standpoint. Same API surface, you pin model versions and change endpoint routing. Operationally you might need a new credentialing step and potential adjustments to autoscaling policies. We support canary rollouts to reduce risk.
03:35 Liam: Any lock-in with custom optimizations? Like if Redwood does quantization that changes semantics?
03:40 Samira: We provide model variant guidance; the runtime optimizations are backward-compatible. There are subtle differences across quantization formats but we surface those in our model catalog and evaluation reports so you can validate.
03:56 Priya: Can we run a simple latency benchmark? e.g., 512 tokens gen, average p50/p95?
04:04 Samira: For hosted, p50 for a 512 ongoing generation on our recommended model is typically ~120-220 ms per token depending on batch, which translates to X ms end-to-end for that prompt size. p95 is more variable. We can run a small benchmark from your region if you want.
04:25 Ethan: Actually region matters. We're based in EU — any hosting in eu-west?
04:30 Jordan: Yes we have EU regions. We'll note eu-west for the pilot and provision region-specific endpoints where possible.
04:36 Nadia: One organizational question: who should be involved from our side for the two-week pilot?
04:40 Jordan: Ideally one engineer, one ML owner, and a product PM to verify success criteria. Looks like you have that set.
04:46 Priya: For success criteria — our list: 1) secure ingestion pipeline with redaction, 2) first-pass assistant answering 70% of QA checks, 3) measurement on latency under 200 ms p50. Is that reasonable?
04:58 Samira: Those are reasonable. For p50 <200 ms, you'll likely want to tune batching and possibly pick a model variant. We'll add guidance and sample config in the quickstart.
05:10 Jordan: Ok quick recap of next steps: we provision credits, send quickstart repo + ingest scripts, Samira will schedule a 60-minute deep dive to run sample benchmarks (SE-led), and Tomas will open the ticket for credits.
05:22 Ethan: Sounds good. Also — compliance: can we do bring-your-own-key (BYOK) for KMS?
05:28 Samira: Yes for dedicated and private deployments BYOK is supported; hosted supports customer-managed KMS in many cases. The security pack has the details.
05:36 Priya: How about data deletion and retention? We need to ensure ephemeral storage for PII in logs.
05:42 Jordan: We have retention controls and you can opt to disable logging at token level for specific projects. We'll share the manual.
05:50 Liam: Who do we ping for limits? Rate limits and quotas if we're testing concurrently?
05:55 Tomas: I'll be the contact. I'll include rate-limit increase steps in the ticket.
06:02 Speaker 1: (interrupt) can you show how the SDK looks like?
06:06 Samira: I'll paste an example in the quickstart. Very short: import SDK, set key, call client.generate with model param. We also have curl snippets and a node/python starter app.
06:20 Ethan: Would you recommend we use streaming or blocking responses for our assistant?
06:25 Samira: For interactive agent UI, streaming is better — lower perceived latency. For batch inference embedding ops, blocking is fine. We can advise based on your UI tests.
06:35 Jordan: Let's talk risk: if we start on hosted and later need private for regulatory reasons, there's a path but it will take additional time — typically 6-10 weeks depending on infra and contracts. We're upfront about that.
06:53 Priya: Ok. Any competitor comparisons relevant to our use?
06:58 Jordan: The usual — OpenAI and Anthropic come up. The main differentiator is our focus on inference economics and predictable unit costs plus a consistent runtime across deployments. We'll send a short competitive note.
07:12 Ethan: Can we get a sample cost estimate for 10k embeddings/day + 50k tokens generation per day?
07:18 Samira: We'll produce a back-of-envelope with the pilot credits applied. I'll include cost per 1k tokens and per-embedding unit in the doc.
07:30 Jordan: Alright, I'll recap the concrete next steps now.
07:33 -- the conversation continues with some clarifying questions, a bit of cross talk, and Samira answering technical specifics.
20:00 Samira: (details about model selection) We recommend starting with a mid-sized open model for cost / quality balance and upgrade if you need lower latency.
25:30 Priya: For ingestion we'll use the open-source vector store we already have, any compatibility issues?
25:36 Samira: No, we support common vector stores and can provide example connectors for Pinecone, Milvus, and our recommended FB-store. (note: transcription may misname stores occasionally)
30:00 Jordan: Final recap: 1) Tomas will provision credits and post quickstart links; 2) Samira to run a one-hour benchmark session (schedule next week); 3) Jordan to share security pack and competitive note; 4) Umbra to nominate pilot engineers and success criteria; 5) follow-up dedicated/private timings only after pilot indicates need.
30:30 Ethan: Great thanks, see you on the benchmark call.
30:34 Jordan: Thanks everyone, talk soon.

(There are pauses, brief cross talk, and a few mis-transcribed product names in the recording, transcription cleans up some but retains authenticity.)
